title: How Apple Really Makes Money (The $479 Billion Machine)
description:
Apple brought in $479 billion in fiscal 2026 — and kept about $132 billion as net profit. In this file we open the money machine behind Apple: a bedroom and a garage in 1976, the $800 sale of a 10% stake, the 1997 near-collapse and comeback, the iPod, iPhone and App Store, the 2.5 billion active devices, the high-margin Services business, the App Store and Google search toll booths, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Apple fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results (Form 8-K exhibit 99.1, November 2026) and Apple Newsroom; Apple fiscal 2025 results press release and earnings call (via Nasdaq, The Motley Fool); MacRumors and 9to5Mac earnings call coverage (installed base, paid subscriptions, margins); AppleInsider (2.35 billion devices, 2025); Apple Newsroom / PocketGamer.biz (App Store ecosystem study, 2026); Yahoo Finance (Google search payments and the 2025 ruling); Parade/AOL (Apple at 50); Neowin and SlashGear (1997 comeback, Microsoft investment); HISTORY (first iPod); iMore (App Store year one); Consumer Reports (first iPhone).

All figures are from company reports where available and are rounded. Segment gross margins, the ~40% Services share of gross profit and the ~28% net margin are our own arithmetic from Apple's reported figures. The Google figure is a court-document estimate for 2022. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
